review_policy: A candidate enters a normative profile only after public review, executable tests, and at least two implementation mappings.

candidates.problem: An approval or credential can become unsafe after issuance, but most agent runs only check access at start time.
candidates.candidate_contract: The credential custodian consumes signed revocation or risk signals, interrupts affected work, and records the last accepted signal and resulting state transition.

candidates.problem: Agent identity, impersonation, and on-behalf-of delegation are frequently collapsed into one bearer credential.
candidates.candidate_contract: The run distinguishes actor and subject, limits audience, scope, resource, and lifetime, and retains token-exchange or delegation evidence without retaining the secret token.

candidates.problem: Agent frameworks measure tokens or cost inconsistently and rarely bind budgets to admission or post-run acceptance.
candidates.candidate_contract: A task declares hard and soft budgets for time, actions, money, tokens, GPU, energy, storage, and network; enforcement and overruns are receipted.

candidates.problem: Canceling one UI or planner process may not stop already delegated or queued effects.
candidates.candidate_contract: A signed stop signal propagates to planners, critics, executors, queues, and UI sessions and closes with an acknowledgement set and unresolved-effect ledger.

candidates.problem: Persistent browsers, sandboxes, caches, skills, and trajectory stores can leak data between tasks or users.
candidates.candidate_contract: Tenant, task, credential, artifact, cache, and retention boundaries are explicit and tested through cross-tenant negative cases.

candidates.problem: An adapter can silently fall back to an older schema or omit a required extension and thereby weaken admission rules.
candidates.candidate_contract: Negotiation binds minimum versions and required extensions; security-relevant downgrade attempts fail and are receipted.

candidates.problem: A portable agent run may move screenshots, prompts, credentials, and artifacts across jurisdictions without machine-readable constraints.
candidates.candidate_contract: Artifacts and processors declare residency, transfer, retention, and deletion constraints that policy can enforce before data movement.

candidates.problem: Approval expiry, leases, event ordering, and non-repudiation depend on clocks that may drift or be controlled by the runtime.
candidates.candidate_contract: Time source, uncertainty, monotonic ordering, and expiry evaluation are declared and attested for security-relevant decisions.

candidates.problem: Semantic, accessibility, and visual routes can expose different controls or effects, creating hidden capability and safety gaps.
candidates.candidate_contract: Fixtures compare available actions, labels, state transitions, and approvals across semantic, accessibility, and visual routes.

candidates.problem: Agents, skills, or generated programs may memorize fixtures, hidden state, or acceptance logic and produce misleading benchmark success.
candidates.candidate_contract: Training and evaluation lineage, hidden-state access, fixture generation, contamination checks, and variant secrecy are retained in the evidence bundle.
